rows.text: After section 7 insert— Temporary class drug orders: power to make further provision This section applies if a temporary class drug order specifies a substance or product as a drug subject to temporary control. Section 31(1) (general provision as to regulations) applies in relation to a temporary class drug order that contains provision made by virtue of this section as it applies to regulations under this Act. .

rows.text: After section 2 insert— Temporary class drug orders The Secretary of State may make an order (referred to in this Act as a “temporary class drug order”) specifying any substance or product as a drug subject to temporary control if the following two conditions are met. The first condition is that the substance or product is not a Class A drug, a Class B drug or a Class C drug. The second condition is that— the Secretary of State has consulted in accordance with section 2B and has determined that the order should be made, or the Secretary of State has received a recommendation under that section that the order should be made. The Secretary of State may make the determination mentioned in subsection (3)(a) only if it appears to the Secretary of State that— the substance or product is a drug that is being, or is likely to be, misused, and that misuse is having, or is capable of having, harmful effects. A substance or product may be specified in a temporary class drug order by reference to— the name of the substance or product, or a description of the substance or product (which may take such form as the Secretary of State thinks appropriate for the purposes of the specification). A substance or product specified in a temporary class drug order as a drug subject to temporary control ceases to be a controlled drug by virtue of the order— at the end of one year beginning with the day on which the order comes into force, or if earlier, upon the coming into force of an Order in Council under section 2(2) by virtue of which the substance or product is specified in Part 1, 2 or 3 of Schedule 2. Subsection (6)— is subject to subsection (10) , and is without prejudice to the power of the Secretary of State to vary or revoke a temporary class drug order by a further order. The power of the Secretary of State to make an order under this section is subject to section 2B. An order under this section is to be made by statutory instrument. An order under this section— must be laid before Parliament after being made, and ceases to have effect at the end of the period of 40 days beginning with the day on which the order is made unless before the end of that period the order is approved by a resolution of each House of Parliament. In calculating that period of 40 days no account is to be taken of any time during which Parliament is dissolved or prorogued or during which both Houses are adjourned for more than 4 days. Subsection (10)(b)— is without prejudice to anything previously done or to the power of the Secretary of State to make a new order under this section; does not apply to an order that only revokes a previous order under this section. Orders under section 2A: role of Advisory Council etc Before making an order under section 2A the Secretary of State— must consult as mentioned in subsection (2), or must have received a recommendation from the Advisory Council to make the order. The Secretary of State must consult— the Advisory Council, or if the order is to be made under section 2A(1) and the urgency condition applies, the person mentioned in subsection (3). The person referred to in subsection (2)(b) is— the person who is for the time being the chairman of the Advisory Council appointed under paragraph 1(3) of Schedule 1, or if that person has delegated the function of responding to consultation under subsection (1)(a) to another member of the Advisory Council, that other member. The “urgency condition” applies if it appears to the Secretary of State that the misuse of the substance or product to be specified in the order as a drug subject to temporary control, or the likelihood of its misuse, poses an urgent and significant threat to public safety or health. The duty of the Advisory Council or any other person consulted under subsection (1)(a) is limited to giving to the Secretary of State that person’s opinion as to whether the order in question should be made. A recommendation under subsection (1)(b) that a temporary class drug order should be made may be given by the Advisory Council only if it appears to the Council that— the substance or product is a drug that is being, or is likely to be, misused, and that misuse is having, or is capable of having, harmful effects. .
